reason: Full v3 HTML text including appendices A-E read; non-weight skill/remedy knowledge store with frozen-store accumulation and cross-tier transfer evidence; scored on a full 8-item basis.

paper.title: MineEvolve: Self-Evolution with Accumulated Knowledge for Long-Horizon Embodied Minecraft Agents
paper.central_claim: MineEvolve: converting typed execution feedback (state/inventory/failure/progress/stagnation) into curated skills and remedies and using them for knowledge-conditioned local plan repair, without updating LM parameters, consistently improves long-horizon Minecraft success across multiple planner LLMs, with larger gains on high-dependency task groups.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model type per claude-kimi config (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

sections_read: Appendix A-E (compute, algorithms 1-3, task suite, Tables 3-10, case studies, prompts)
missing_sections: Figure 4/5 bar and curve values are images not present in the text material (numbers recovered only from Tables 2, 4, 6)

evidence.quote: a knowledge-driven self-evolution framework that converts execution feedback into actionable behavioral knowledge
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim and retained object (external behavioral knowledge).

evidence.quote: existing methods mostly focus on successful skill reuse, historical summaries, or dependency correction, while the conversion of fine-grained execution feedback into behavioral knowledge for plan repair remains underexplored.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap with named neighbours (Voyager, Optimus-1, XENON, Reflexion family).

evidence.quote: without updating the parameters of the language model
evidence.support_explanation: Retention is purely in an external non-weight store; in scope.

evidence.quote: each field in this representation comes from environment states, inventory changes, or execution monitors, and can therefore be directly used by the knowledge generation process.
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback signal is environment-derived, not self-judged.

evidence.quote: This condition prevents a single accidental failure from being immediately stored as a remedy, while still allowing repeated failure patterns or clear stagnation to be captured.
evidence.support_explanation: Remedy induction requires repeated failure or stagnation (windowed rate threshold).

evidence.quote: Only accepted candidates are written into the external knowledge store; otherwise, they remain only as feedback records for the current episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit accept/reject gate (schema, match, exec, specificity, conflict) before persistence.

evidence.quote: Each entry contains a trigger context, knowledge content, supporting feedback, confidence, support count, and usage history.
evidence.support_explanation: Entries carry provenance, support counts and usage history; no stated retirement rule.

evidence.quote: Curator first filters out non-executable, overly generic, or conflicting candidates, and then retrieves the most relevant knowledge under a fixed prompt budget.
evidence.support_explanation: Curator duties; filtering and bounded retrieval.

evidence.quote: You are the Curator module of MineEvolve. Validate candidate skill/remedy entries
evidence.support_explanation: The Curator gate is an LLM prompt, so executability and conflict checks are model-judged rather than replayed in the environment.

evidence.quote: Under the unified MC task protocol, MineEvolve achieves the highest Overall and Hard Avg. across multiple planner backbones.
evidence.support_explanation: Main result claim; Table 4 shows margins from +0.37 (GLM-4.7 overall vs Optimus-2) to +3.27 (GPT-5.5), with no variance reported.

evidence.quote: All compared methods are evaluated on the same task set, task–seed split, episode horizon, success criterion, and success-rate metric.
evidence.support_explanation: Protocol control across baselines, with Optimus-2 using a different native low-level policy.

evidence.quote: is the number of evaluation runs for task
evidence.support_explanation: R_t is only symbolic; the actual number of runs per task is not stated.

evidence.quote: we freeze the external knowledge base at different experience scales and evaluate on held-out hard tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Store-frozen evaluation at 0/50/100/200/400 episodes against Static Store and Text Reflection controls.

evidence.quote: During evaluation, no further knowledge is updated or generated.
evidence.support_explanation: Separates retained knowledge from online adaptation during evaluation.

evidence.quote: Values denote SR (%) on held-out hard tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 6 Hard Avg at 400 episodes: Static Store 28.22, Text Reflection 29.56, MineEvolve 35.02, all from 25.13 at 0 episodes.

evidence.quote: This result shows that knowledge induced from lower-tier tasks, including tool crafting, resource collection, smelting, crafting prerequisites, and common failure-recovery patterns, can transfer to Diamond tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Frozen lower-tier knowledge reaches 16.4% on Diamond vs 2.9% empty KB, a cross-task-group transfer result.

evidence.quote: Each evaluation is repeated across multiple world seeds, and the success rate is averaged over the seven Diamond tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Number of seeds unstated; Diamond-only self-learning is evaluated on the same Diamond tasks it learned from, so 'held-out' there is seed-level only.

evidence.quote: Typed Execution Feedback substantially outperforms both binary feedback and trajectory-level reflection across all difficult task groups.
evidence.support_explanation: Hard Avg 27.06 (binary), 29.98 (trajectory reflection), 37.13 (typed); key feedback-granularity control under matched KB size and LLM-call budget.

evidence.quote: Static Store freezes the knowledge base and is used to examine whether continuous knowledge updates truly bring self-evolutionary gains.
evidence.support_explanation: Store-off/frozen-store control is part of the ablation set (plus w/o Curator, w/o Adaptor, Skills Only, Remedies Only).

evidence.quote: reports the knowledge-base size, retrieval tokens, retrieval latency, and the number of evaluation-time LLM calls
evidence.support_explanation: Table 7: eval-time LLM calls 7.82 to 8.31 and retrieved tokens up to 1216; accumulation-phase LLM/env cost is not reported.

evidence.quote: relies on environment-specific execution signals, such as inventory changes, GUI states, crafting progress, and failure types
evidence.support_explanation: Typed feedback fields are hand-engineered for Minecraft; generality untested.

evidence.quote: We evaluate MineEvolve on a 70-task subset selected from the Minecraft MCU tech-tree benchmark
evidence.support_explanation: Subset of 70 tasks; selection criteria and per-group task counts (6 to 16) given only in appendix Table 3.

evidence.quote: we do not train the planner backbone or STEVE-1.
evidence.support_explanation: No weight training confounds the comparison.

signatures.object: External knowledge store K of skills and remedies (trigger, preconditions/repair, verification, confidence, support, usage)
signatures.information: Typed execution feedback from environment state diffs, inventory diffs, failure type, progress and stagnation flag; no labels beyond task success checks
signatures.operation: Monitor builds typed feedback; Inducer (LLM) makes skills from verified successful segments and remedies from repeated failure/stagnation; Curator validates (schema, match, exec, specificity, conflict), merges or inserts, retrieves under token budget
signatures.output: Curated entries injected into planner prompts and used by Adaptor
signatures.conditions: Failure-rate threshold over window h, stagnation threshold, PassTargetCheck for skills; threshold values not given in text
signatures.selection_rule_data: Rule-based plus LLM-judged acceptance; no marginal-utility test per entry
signatures.persistence: K persists across episodes; merge exists; retirement/rollback not described
signatures.later_use: Retrieved at planning time and at repair time for suffix replanning
signatures.claimed_effect: Hard Avg and Overall gains over DEPS, JARVIS-1, Optimus-1/2 on five planners; Table 6 accumulation curve
signatures.failure_boundary: Environment-specific feedback fields; margin small on easy groups and some planners

signatures.information: Retrieved skills, active remedies, temporary remedy from current failure
signatures.operation: Adaptor freezes completed prefix and regenerates only the suffix when repeated failure or stagnation is detected
signatures.persistence: Per episode; knowledge effect persists via K
signatures.later_use: Subsequent execution in the same episode
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o Adaptor ablation drops (Fig 4, values not in text)

gap.author_gap: Prior Minecraft agents retrieve raw trajectories, reuse static successes or rely on generic text reflection, giving weak guidance for repairing failures.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and testable: feedback granularity and knowledge form are the changed non-weight objects; Table 2 and the Text Reflection control address it directly.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Voyager (code skill library), Optimus-1 (hybrid memory), XENON (knowledge revision), Reflexion-type reflection; cited in Sec 2.3, v3. Generic skill-library work outside Minecraft is only partly covered.
gap.residue: Fine-grained feedback to plan-repair knowledge was thin among Minecraft neighbours.
gap.stakes: Long-horizon dependency chains fail on missing prerequisites and stagnation; hard groups have 2-30% success.
gap.method_response: Typed feedback, skill/remedy induction, curated store, suffix repair.
gap.remaining_gap: Typed fields hand-built per environment; no retirement/admission-by-utility; Minecraft only; absolute hard-task SR still low.
unresolved: Whether Optimus-2 differences reflect the low-level policy

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C03: retrieved (state, outcome, action)-style reference bank (skills/remedies with triggers) conditions a frozen planner at inference with no parameter update (met); upstream phase teaching format parsing is absent because LLM planners read JSON entries zero-shot; substrate breadth limited to one environment.
matches.success_failure_checks: Ablation toggling the conditioning store (Static Store, Cold Start) met; obvious cheaper alternative (Text Reflection, trajectory retrieval baselines) met; generic across tasks/domains unmet (Minecraft only).
matches.reason: Inference-time conditioning on a curated bank is the executed operation; the construction side (induction and curation) goes beyond the card.

rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partially: hard-task SR rises with frozen stores, but absolute levels remain low and only Minecraft is tested

matches.condition_checks: S3 grounding signal met; S5 gate met (quality filters); S4 maintenance partial (merge, conflict, budget but no forgetting); S2 contrast partial.
Remedies are trigger-conditioned lessons from failures with typed grounding; F2 'new domain is novelty' partial.
Admission checks present; no marginal-gain/counterfactual test, no retirement or quarantine.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Retrieval of curated skills/remedies into a frozen planner prompt corresponds to retrieving and injecting guidance from a living store.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_differences: H01 additionally requires explicit edit operations (merge, conflict filter present; delete/forget absent here); C03 upstream training of format reading is replaced by zero-shot LLM reading.

expectations.applies_when: stored knowledge conditions a frozen model
expectations.reason: Cold Start/0-episode, Static Store and Text Reflection controls isolate the conditioning signal.
Task-seed split and frozen-store evaluation described, but held-out status of tasks versus accumulation episodes is unclear and LLM planner prior knowledge of Minecraft recipes is unaudited.
Compared to trajectory/case retrieval systems (JARVIS-1, Optimus-1), static store and free-form reflection.
Monitor/Inducer/Curator/Adaptor each have an ablation variant under matched budgets (values for Fig 4 not in text).
Single environment; feedback fields are Minecraft-specific.
Store-size sweep (0-400 episodes) and construction pathway comparison exist, but no noise or low-quality entry injection.
Skills from successes and remedies from failures are produced separately; no explicit paired contrast of success and failure on the same situation.
Environment-derived typed signals (state/inventory) decide skill vs remedy.
Merge, conflict filter and token-budgeted retrieval exist; no forgetting threshold or retirement of stale entries.
Five-part Curator acceptance rule precedes persistence, though judged by an LLM.
Minecraft application of act-reflect-store-retrieve, but typed feedback and suffix repair are distinguished by controls (Table 2).
Support count and usage history are stored but no counterfactual with/without entry credit is computed.
Admission only; no retirement rule or size bound beyond retrieval budget (KB grows to 143 skills and 191 remedies).
Fixed prompt budget B (512 tokens in the prompt example) and relevance retrieval.
No seeds, intervals or run counts; some margins are under 1 point (GLM-4.7 overall).
Cross-tier frozen transfer (Table 9) is true task-group transfer; Table 6 and Diamond-only learning use unclear or same-task evaluation.

expectations.applies_when: executability and conflict checks claimed as validation
expectations.reason: Validation is performed by an LLM Curator, not by replaying skills in the environment before admission.

claims.text: MineEvolve achieves highest Overall and Hard Avg across five planner LLMs on a 70-task MCU subset.
claims.setting: STEVE-1 low-level policy; same task-seed split, horizon, retrieval/LLM-call budgets for STEVE-1 baselines
claims.baseline_control: DEPS, JARVIS-1, Optimus-1 (same policy), Optimus-2 (GOAP policy)
claims.selection_vs_test: Task-seed split stated; whether knowledge persists across test episodes in Table 1 is not stated
claims.result_denominator: Task-weighted SR; run count R_t unspecified; no variance
claims.allowed_conclusion: Higher reported mean SR; margins small on some planners and uncertainty unknown.

claims.text: Typed feedback and structured skills/remedies, not just reflection, drive the gain.
claims.setting: Qwen3.5-Plus; matched KB size, retrieval budget, replanning trigger and LLM-call budget
claims.baseline_control: Binary feedback, trajectory-level reflection, Text Reflection, Skills Only, Remedies Only, w/o Curator, w/o Adaptor, Static Store
claims.result_denominator: Hard Avg 27.06 / 29.98 / 37.13 (Table 2); Fig 4 values not in text
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within Minecraft hard tasks, typed feedback outperforms binary and trajectory reflection under matched budgets.

claims.text: Accumulated knowledge improves held-out hard-task performance and transfers across task tiers.
claims.setting: Frozen KB at 0-400 episodes; curriculum pretraining then freeze
claims.baseline_control: Static Store, Text Reflection, Cold Start
claims.selection_vs_test: KB frozen at evaluation; held-out definition partly unclear
claims.result_denominator: Hard Avg 25.13 to 35.02 vs 28.22 and 29.56; Diamond 2.9 vs 16.4
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retained knowledge improves later hard-task SR in this environment; transfer across tiers shown on Diamond only.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In Minecraft MCU hard task groups, a curated store of typed-feedback skills and remedies, frozen at evaluation, raises later success rates versus static-store and text-reflection controls, with some cross-tier transfer; improver-level self-improvement and cross-environment generality are not shown.
unresolved: role of different low-level policy in Optimus-2 comparison

G.reason: Specific fixed objects (feedback granularity, knowledge form) with named neighbours and a direct test; residual is clear but lineage outside Minecraft is thin.

M.reason: Typed feedback to trigger-conditioned skill/remedy to suffix repair is a coherent chain with distinguishable predictions (binary vs typed vs reflection), though the typed fields are hand-engineered.

X.reason: Pseudocode, schemas, acceptance rule, retrieval budget and repair scope are reconstructable; retirement, rollback and threshold values are missing and validation is LLM-judged.

E.measurement.reason: Success is checked from game state on an established tech-tree benchmark with task-weighted aggregation; 70-task subset selection and baseline re-implementation add some uncertainty.

E.causality.reason: Store-off/frozen-store, free-form-reflection, feedback-granularity and per-module ablations under matched KB, retrieval and LLM-call budgets; no alternative improver (e.g. Voyager-style library) run on the same protocol and Fig 4 values unavailable.

E.holdout.reason: Frozen-store evaluation and cross-tier transfer exist, but held-out status of tasks versus accumulation episodes is unclear, Diamond-only learning re-tests the same tasks, and planner prior Minecraft knowledge is unaudited.

E.statistics.reason: Task counts and some losses are shown, but run counts are symbolic, seed count unstated, and no intervals or tests despite sub-point margins.

E.cost.reason: Evaluation-time LLM-call and retrieval budgets matched and reported (Table 7), but knowledge-construction cost over 400 episodes is not reported.
